 NECESSITY FOR THE BELL COUNTY EAST                          §
 SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV                        §        COMMISSION OF
 TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT IN BELL,                          §
 BURNET, CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                          §        TEXAS
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH, MENARD,                            §
 MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM                     §
 GREEN AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                               §



TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

Intervenor George Noelke submits this Brief on Remanded Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13
pursuant to SOAH Order No. 35, as made applicable to Intervenors in Docket No. 59182 by the
Administrative Law Judges’ rulings in Order 36 (59475) and Order 28 (59182).


I. PRELIMINARY STATEMENT & RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

This brief is submitted under special appearance and is expressly subject to, and without waiver of,
Intervenor’s pending Motion to Dismiss for Want of Jurisdiction in Docket No. 59182 based on the lapse
 of the mandatory statutory 180-day deadline under PURA § 37.057. Nothing herein shall be construed as
a general appearance or as a waiver of that fatal jurisdictional defect in 59182.

This submission is further subject to, and without waiver of:
1. Intervenor’s Objection and Motion to Strike Applicants’ "Directory of Evidence" filed on September
22, 2026 (Item No. 6595 in Docket No. 59475 / Item No. 615 in Docket No. 59182);
2. All procedural objections regarding the asymmetric scope of the limited consolidation between Docket
Nos. 59475 and 59182, including questions regarding party standing and the participation of non-parties;
and
3. Intervenor Kevin Kennedy’s Appeal of SOAH Order No. 35 and Request for Commission-Directed
Independent Technical Investigation and Forensic Audit, filed on September 23, 2026, pursuant to 16
TAC § 22.123.

If the Commission ballots and grants Kennedy’s appeal, the proceedings in both 59475 and 59182 should
be abated pending completion of that audit. However, because the ALJs have ruled that the evidentiary
record remains closed and ordered briefing under Order No. 35, Intervenor submits this brief to
demonstrate that even on the existing, closed evidentiary record, Applicants have completely failed to
carry their burden of proof on both remanded issues.

II. PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUE NO. 11: APPLICANTS FAILED TO PROVE THE
PROPOSED FACILITIES ARE NECESSARY TO MEET STATE OR FEDERAL RELIABILITY
STANDARDS

Preliminary Order Issue No. 11 asks: "Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or
federal reliability standards?"

Applicants contend that ERCOT’s recommendations in the Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP) are
entitled to "great weight" under 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii)(II). However, regulatory deference cannot
substitute for substantial evidence when federal reliability standards are directly at issue. The closed
record establishes that Applicants have failed to carry their burden of proof.

A. Applicants Concede the PBRP Was Never Intended to Demonstrate Compliance with NERC
Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1
Throughout the evidentiary hearing and in their September 21 "Directory of Evidence," Applicants
repeatedly asserted that the PBRP reliability assessments proved necessity under North American Electric
Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1 (Directory at 3–5).

However, in their formal Response to Kevin Kennedy’s Appeal of SOAH Order No. 35, filed on
September 30, 2026, Applicants made a fatal concession regarding the scope of the PBRP:
"Finally, Mr. Kennedy's argument that the PBRP must comply with NERC Reliability Standard
TPL-001-5.1 conflates the requirements applicable to ERCOT's annual planning assessment (the RTP)
with those applicable to special-purpose studies. ... Special ERCOT studies like the PBRP are not required
to, and generally are not intended to, independently demonstrate compliance with NERC Reliability
Standard TPL-001-5.1. They are focused on achieving a study scope for a specific purpose. Here, the


                                                                                                            1
 purpose is the legislative mandate under H.B. 5066 to develop a reliability plan for the Permian Basin."
(Applicants' Response to Appeal at 8).

This admission resolves Issue No. 11. Issue No. 11 does not inquire whether the proposed facilities satisfy
an economic or regional policy mandate under House Bill 5066; it asks specifically whether the facilities
are necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards. By conceding that the PBRP was a
"special-purpose study" neither required nor intended to demonstrate compliance with NERC Standard
TPL-001-5.1, Applicants admit that their primary study cannot answer Preliminary Order Issue No. 11.​

B. Applicants’ Pleading Concession Constitutes an Opposing Party Admission and Binding Judicial
Admission
Under Tex. R. Evid. 801(e)(2)(D), applicable to this proceeding pursuant to Tex. Gov't Code § 2001.081
and 1 TAC § 155.429(a)(1), Applicants’ written statements in formal pleadings signed by counsel
constitute substantive admissions of an opposing party. Moreover, because Applicants’ statement in their
September 30, 2026 Response at page 8—conceding that special-purpose studies like the PBRP are not
intended to independently demonstrate compliance with NERC Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1—is
clear, deliberate, and unequivocal, it constitutes a binding judicial admission under Texas law. See Holy
Cross Church of God in Christ v. Wolf, 44 S.W.3d 562, 568 (Tex. 2001); Houston First Am. Sav. Ass'n v.
Musick, 650 S.W.2d 764, 767 (Tex. 1983) (holding that assertions of fact in live formal filings bar the
asserting party from disputing the admitted fact). Applicants are bound by this admission, which
establishes on the face of the record that their foundational study was never intended to satisfy the federal
standard required by Preliminary Order Issue No. 11.


C. The Record Contains No Steady-State Contingency Studies Isolating the 765-kV Import Paths
NERC Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1 Requirement R3 mandates steady-state contingency analysis
using computer simulation models. The PBRP performed steady-state contingency evaluations solely for
local Permian Basin upgrades (Applicants' Ex. 1, Att. 5 at 15–16). For the 765-kV import paths, ERCOT
performed only a limited dynamic stability screening (id. at 13–14). Dynamic stability screenings do not
fulfill the steady-state contingency simulation requirements of TPL-001-5.1.

Furthermore, Applicants’ own planning witness admitted under cross-examination that ERCOT never
conducted an engineering study isolating the reliability need for each individual 765-kV import line:
"I am not aware that — aware of a study that isolated each line independently as they were they were
studied together." (Tr. Vol. 2 at 44:21–45:4, Gurley Cross).

An unsegregated, multi-line portfolio analysis fails to establish that this specific project—Import Path
2—is independently necessary to meet mandatory reliability standards.

D. Subsequent Planning Models Merely Assumed the Facilities as Day-One Topology
Attempting to cure the PBRP's admitted deficiencies, Applicants point to the 2024 and 2025 Regional
Transmission Plans (RTP) (Directory at 8–10). But the record confirms that neither RTP independently
proved the necessity of Import Path 2. Instead, ERCOT embedded the entire 765-kV Strategic
Transmission Expansion Plan (STEP) directly into its starting base cases:


                                                                                                            2
 "The 2025 RTP included the entire 765-kV STEP in its 2030 and 2031 starting base cases to address base
case violations and found it provided continued benefits in addressing new load growth." (Applicants' Ex.
17, Ex. JG-R-3 at 28 of 58).

Assuming a multi-billion-dollar project exists as starting topology in a base case does not prove that the
line was necessary to resolve an underlying NERC criteria violation; it merely confirms that power flows
through it once inserted. Such circular modeling cannot satisfy Applicants' burden under Issue No. 11.

E. Evidentiary Conclusion on Issue No. 11
Because the closed evidentiary record lacks any steady-state contingency study isolating the reliability
necessity of Import Path 2, and because Applicants formally concede that the PBRP was not intended to
independently demonstrate compliance with NERC Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1, any affirmative
finding of necessity on Issue No. 11 would lack the requisite support of substantial evidence and would
fail to demonstrate the rational connection required between the record facts and the agency's conclusions.


III. PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUE NO. 13: THE RECORD CONTAINS NO ESTIMATED
CONSUMER CONGESTION COST SAVINGS ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE PROPOSED
FACILITIES

Preliminary Order Issue No. 13 requires the ALJs to identify: "What is the estimated congestion cost
savings for consumers that may result from the proposed transmission facilities considering both current
and future expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce
those congestion levels?"

Applicants have suffered a complete failure of proof under this standard.

A. Total Absence of Project-Specific Consumer Savings Evidence
Under PURA § 37.056, CCN applications must be supported by evidence demonstrating the statutory
factors for the specific transmission facilities applied for. In their 22-page Directory of Evidence,
Applicants fail to cite a single empirical calculation, power-flow dispatch run, or dollar figure quantifying
consumer congestion cost savings attributable specifically to either:
1. The Bell County East to Big Hill segment (Docket No. 59475); or
2. The Big Hill to Sand Lake segment (Docket No. 59182).

Applicants instead cite general, macro-level ERCOT congestion rent figures from 2023 ($2.3 billion) and
2024 ($1.97 billion) and cite generic commentary from the Independent Market Monitor (Directory at 15,
18). Broad system-wide congestion data across 30,000 miles of Texas grid does not demonstrate what
portion, if any, will be saved by consumers by constructing these specific 765-kV segments.

B. System-Wide Comparisons Demonstrate an Insurmountable Economic Deficit for Consumers
The only prospective congestion analysis Applicants cite is Table 1.3.3 from ERCOT's 2024 RTP
comparison (Applicants' Ex. 3, Ex. JG-4 at 19). That table compares the entire statewide 765-kV plan
against a 345-kV alternative for the distant study year of 2039:


                                                                                                             3
 - Incremental annual statewide production cost savings: $28 million;
- Incremental annual statewide consumer energy cost savings: $229 million;
- Incremental annual statewide congestion rent reduction: $172 million.

Weighing an estimated $229 million in speculative, delayed system-wide consumer energy savings in
2039 against the colossal capital expenditure required—approximately $4 billion for Import Path 2 alone,
and between $11 billion and $24 billion for the full 765-kV plan—proves that the project is an economic
net negative for Texas consumers. Ratepayers must service the capital carrying costs, depreciation, and
utility return on investment for billions of dollars in new rate base. The modest, long-delayed congestion
savings cited by Applicants are dwarfed by the massive capital cost pass-throughs ratepayers will bear.

IV. CONCLUSION & PRAYER

On the closed evidentiary record before the State Office of Administrative Hearings, Applicants have
failed to satisfy their burden of proof on both remanded issues:
1. Applicants concede that the PBRP was never intended to demonstrate compliance with NERC
Reliability Standard TPL-001-5.1, and the record contains no steady-state studies isolating the necessity
of Import Path 2; and
2. The record contains zero evidence quantifying consumer congestion cost savings attributable
specifically to the proposed facilities.

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Intervenor George Noelke respectfully requests that the
Administrative Law Judges:
1. Abate these proceedings by delaying the issuance of a remand PFD until the Kennedy appeal has been
formally decided by the PUC;
2. Enter NEGATIVE FINDINGS on Preliminary Order Issue Nos. 11 and 13;
3. Conclude that Applicants failed to meet their burden of establishing that the proposed facilities are
necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards;
4. Conclude that Applicants failed to meet their burden of establishing estimated consumer congestion
cost savings resulting from the proposed facilities; and
5. Reaffirm the 59475 PFD's original recommendation that the applications in Docket Nos. 59475 and
59182 be DENIED.

Dated: October 7, 2026

Respectfully submitted,​
George Noelke​
George Noelke​
Intervenor​
Pro se Landowner
